summary: Robotics engineer (M.S. Computer Engineering, RIT, 2026) who builds robots end to end: perception on NVIDIA Jetson, kinematics and planning, and the firmware that drives the joints. Delivered a voice-commanded, vision-guided pick-and-place arm with 100% pick reliability.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Trained a YOLOv3 ball detector from scratch and turned its detections into motor commands for closed-loop visual servoing of the competition robot.
Led a 25-member robotics team through national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication and AI integration end to end.

experience.title: Research Intern (Capstone)
bullets: Deployed ZoeDepth monocular depth estimation for crack-depth profiling with ±8% error on 3D surface reconstruction.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — M.S. Capstone, RIT
bullets: Architected a voice-controlled, vision-guided pick-and-place robot as a three-layer distributed system: Flutter mobile client, Flask-SocketIO edge server, and an NVIDIA Jetson + Arduino controller on one real-time WebSocket fabric.

Integrated faster-whisper speech-to-text (1.0–1.4 s), Gemini intent classification (<500 ms) and TensorRT-optimized YOLO for visual servoing, accelerating detection 5.2× over eager PyTorch (56.7 → 10.9 ms, 17.6 → 92 FPS).

Implemented two-link inverse kinematics in C++ on the Arduino, driving five servos with contact-aware grasping from dual time-of-flight sensors on an I2C multiplexer: a camera range gate plus a gripper that closes at 25 mm.
Drove the system to 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5 s voice-to-pick by hardening it against false-positive detections, servo brown-out and stale-frame capture.

projects.name: ROS-Based Robotic Arm (AL5B & UR5e)
bullets: Derived DH tables and full forward-kinematic chains by hand for a 6-DoF UR5e and a 5-DoF AL5B, validated against MoveIt and RViz URDF models in ROS 2 Humble and ROS Noetic.
Planned and executed collision-free pick-and-place on the physical UR5e through the UR ROS 2 driver; AL5B repeatability under 2 mm over 10 trials.

projects.name: Autonomous Driving in CARLA
bullets: Trained YOLO11n (mAP50 ~0.85) and fine-tuned UFLD (ResNet-18), integrated into an adaptive control stack with lane following and waypoint fallback.

projects.name: Robocon Competition Robot — Holonomic Drive & Encoder Odometry
bullets: Built closed-loop heading correction for a four-wheel holonomic robot on Arduino Due, deriving heading from dual-axis quadrature-encoder odometry (2400 CPR) and feeding the angular error back into rotation PWM.
